question: 24 tiles; orange box = the note detector's box at its exact size (1-13: every half note written from a too-wide box on a black-class box; 14-24: wide boxes at random). Which numbered boxes are on a real notehead?
verbatim: 6 of the orange boxes are actual notes nothing else is. I feel like many of those should have been ink that was already claimed and most of the boxes are just poorly sized or poorly placed boxes...
answer: 6 of the 24 boxes are on actual notes; the other 18 are not. He did not say which six.
ours: The cutting agent's own look also found six 'one head' boxes: tiles 4, 8, 10, 12, 13, 23 -- the count matches, the identity is NOT confirmed by Sean. His two hypotheses, to be traced not assumed: (1) much of the ink under the 18 should already have been claimed by a page-wide reader (slur, stem, beam, ledger line, tremolo, dynamic) before a head box could take it; (2) most of these boxes are poorly sized or placed. By the record, 7 of tiles 1-13 were made by our own split / rescue steps. FOLLOW-UP 2026-11-26: Sean names five notes (4, 8, 10, 12, 23) and says tile 13 is part of an ff; he had said six, so one of his six is not identified. Tile 13 (Litolff glyph/16/0/0/7/6) is written today as a plain F4 half: a second ff written as a note (the first: Litolff glyph/4/1/7/4/18).

follow_up.asked: The agent's look counted six: 4, 8, 10, 12, 13, 23. Are those your six?
